purpose: Provide deterministic admission, allocation, prioritization, concurrency, queue, scheduling, throttling, suspension, and process-limit enforcement for profile, component, artifact-class, workspace, and workload resource envelopes.

scope.profile_specific_limits_owner: the active deployment profile and active resource envelope artifacts
scope.implementation_mechanism_owner: the active profile and applicable platform toolchain

owns.active_resource_envelope_state: The verified set of active resource envelopes and their resolved precedence for each governed target.
owns.workload_admission_state: Admission outcomes for workload requests based on active envelopes, current capacity, declared criticality, priority, and concurrency.
owns.resource_allocation_state: Current reservations, allocations, leases, limits, and execution bindings created by Resource Governor.
owns.resource_queue_state: Pending workload metadata, ordering, priority, capacity, expiry, retry, cancellation, and dequeue decisions for queues owned by Resource Governor.
owns.resource_scheduling_state: Deterministic scheduling, throttling, suspension, resumption, and rejection decisions made within active envelopes.
owns.resource_usage_observations: Resource-governance observations required to compare actual usage against active limits without owning workload business content.
owns.resource_decision_interfaces: Observable request, decision, allocation, queue, pressure, usage, release, event, and receipt payload semantics defined by this contract.

does_not_own.owner_ref: the active deployment profile and component contract
the active profile and applicable platform toolchain

responsibilities: Resolve the active resource envelope applicable to a target workload.
Validate resource envelope structure, target scope, compatibility, and precedence before activation.
Admit, queue, throttle, defer, or reject workload requests deterministically.
Apply CPU, memory, I/O, process, worker, queue, and concurrency limits through the active profile's enforcement mechanisms.
Preserve required and higher-priority capabilities before optional and task-activated work during pressure.
Track active reservations, allocations, leases, and execution bindings.
Observe governed resource usage without reading or owning workload business content.
Detect envelope violations, capacity pressure, queue saturation, and orphaned execution state.
Suspend, resume, terminate, or reject work only within declared resource authority.
Publish structured resource decisions, pressure events, health state, and required receipts.
Reconcile active controls, workloads, queues, reservations, and envelopes during recovery.
Fail closed for new heavy or unconstrained work when enforceable limits cannot be established.
non_responsibilities: Making business, identity, policy, consent, disclosure, privilege, publication, or conformance decisions.
Deciding whether a workload is legally, ethically, culturally, or organizationally authorized.
Owning or modifying workload business data.
Inventing resource limits when no active envelope resolves.
Treating measured capacity as permission to execute an unauthorized workload.
Treating policy authorization as proof that sufficient resources exist.
Replacing an operating-system scheduler, container runtime, queue broker, or workload executor as an implementation.
Requiring one universal operating-system, cgroup, container, orchestration, or virtualization mechanism.
Guaranteeing application-level correctness after a workload is terminated or suspended.
Activating production Release Sets solely because resource checks pass.

authority_boundary.resource_authority: Resource Governor may decide whether and when an already authorized workload can consume resources within active envelopes.
authority_boundary.policy_authority: Governance Policy Runtime decides governed authorization, disclosure, consent, privilege, and exceptions where required.
separation_rules: A resource admission decision does not authorize the workload's business operation.
A policy approval does not reserve or guarantee resources.
Resource Governor does not infer policy from priority, capacity, queue position, or requester identity.
Governance Policy Runtime does not alter resource allocations directly.
A workload requiring both authorities proceeds only after both independent decisions pass.

accelerators.profile_condition: used only when the active profile and workload contract declare accelerator support

resource_envelope_contract.role: A versioned declaration of resource limits and scheduling constraints for a profile, profile overlay, component, artifact class, workspace, or workload class.
required_semantics: queue capacity, ordering, expiry, retry, and cancellation policy
precedence: individual workload request within all enclosing limits
resource_envelope_contract.resolution_rule: The most specific applicable envelope may strengthen or further restrict an enclosing envelope but cannot exceed or weaken an enclosing hard boundary.

preconditions: all referenced units and dimensions are supported
limits remain within the active profile capability
required owner decision and evidence resolve
activation.failed_activation_effect: the previous verified envelope remains active

envelope_resolution.description: Resolve the complete active envelope chain for a governed target.
envelope_resolution.failure_behavior: Block new governed work for targets whose enforceable envelope cannot be resolved.

workload_admission.description: Admit, queue, defer, or reject workload requests using active limits and current capacity.
workload_admission.failure_behavior: Block new heavy or unconstrained work; preserve bounded existing work when controls remain verifiable.

runtime_enforcement.description: Apply resolved resource controls through profile-selected enforcement adapters.
runtime_enforcement.failure_behavior: Block new affected work and stop or safely constrain nonconforming execution according to the active envelope.

priority_scheduling.description: Order eligible work deterministically by criticality, priority, fairness, deadlines, and declared queue policy.
priority_scheduling.failure_behavior: Pause dequeue and preserve durable queue state until deterministic ordering can be restored.

concurrency_control.description: Enforce concurrent workload, worker, process, and heavy-job limits.
concurrency_control.failure_behavior: Reject or queue new work rather than weakening concurrency limits.

queue_management.description: Own pending-work metadata for queues explicitly delegated to Resource Governor.
queue_management.condition: the workload contract permits durable queuing
queue_management.failure_behavior: Reject new queue submissions when durability or capacity cannot be guaranteed.

pressure_degradation.description: Reduce resource use while preserving required capabilities and active authority boundaries.
pressure_degradation.failure_behavior: Block new nonessential work when no safe degraded action can be selected.

resource_observability.description: Expose current envelope, allocation, queue, usage, pressure, and enforcement state.
resource_observability.failure_behavior: Do not claim healthy enforcement when required observations are unavailable.

input_factors: deadline, expiry, retry, and cancellation rules

outcomes.admitted: Resources are reserved and an execution binding may be created.
outcomes.queued: The valid request is durably retained for later reevaluation.
outcomes.deferred: The request is returned without queue ownership and may be resubmitted.
outcomes.rejected: The request cannot execute under current or declared constraints.
outcomes.blocked: Required authority, envelope, identity, compatibility, or enforcement cannot be resolved.

rules: Admission is deterministic for the same verified state and inputs.
Admission does not authorize the business action performed by the workload.
A queued request is reevaluated against current policy and resource authority before execution.
An expired, cancelled, superseded, or unauthorized queued request is not executed.
Priority never overrides a hard limit or missing authority.
Capacity availability never creates undeclared profile or component capability.

scheduling_model.determinism: Ties are resolved through a stable registered ordering rule and never through an unrecorded random or provider-controlled decision.

conditions: the active envelope permits suspension or termination
the workload contract defines safe interruption behavior
required state is checkpointed or explicitly disposable
the preemption action remains within resource authority
prohibited_when: the workload is in a registered non-interruptible critical section
no declared recovery or termination behavior exists

scheduling_model.fairness: Fairness applies within active criticality and hard boundaries; it does not force equal resource allocation across unequal declared priorities.

queue_contract.authority: Resource Governor owns only queue and delivery metadata for queues delegated to it; the workload owner retains authority over the requested domain action.
rules: Queue capacity is finite and enforced.
Queue persistence matches the workload's durability requirement.
Expiry and cancellation are evaluated before dequeue.
Authorization and resource authority are reevaluated before execution.
Duplicate execution is prevented or the workload contract declares idempotency.
Queue exhaustion rejects or defers new work without silently dropping accepted items.
A queue item never becomes an authoritative domain object.

resource_decision_receipt.emission: Required for resource-envelope activation, governed override, forced termination, emergency degradation, and other policy-classified critical transitions.

authoritative_stores.content: active envelope identities, versions, targets, precedence, activation state, and rollback references
reservations, allocations, execution bindings, leases, limits, and release state
queue items and delivery metadata for queues explicitly delegated to Resource Governor

observational_data.authority: measurement of governed resource use only
observed capacity at a recorded time; not a future guarantee
resource pressure evidence; not policy authorization

prohibited_data_actions: reading workload business content to determine resource admission
using queue metadata as a domain transaction record
retaining credentials not required for resource-control interfaces
treating cached measurements as current capacity without freshness validation
altering a resource envelope artifact in place

required_local.role: provide profile hardware and capability boundaries

required_local.failure_behavior: block new affected work; existing verified controls may remain active

required_local.role: apply resource controls through the active platform
required_local.failure_behavior: block new work requiring unavailable enforcement

required_local.role: bind controls to the intended process, container, service, workspace, worker, or job
required_local.failure_behavior: block or terminate the unbound execution according to the active envelope

required_local.role: provide measurements required to verify enforcement
required_local.failure_behavior: do not claim healthy enforcement; block work that cannot be safely bounded

conditional.condition: activation or override requires actor identity or trust verification
envelope activation, override, termination, or exception requires a governed decision
conditional.failure_behavior: block the governed transition; Resource Governor does not infer approval

conditional.condition: the resource transition requires an immutable receipt
conditional.failure_behavior: do not commit a receipt-before-commit transition when persistence is unavailable

conditional.condition: a delegated queue requires durable pending-work state
conditional.failure_behavior: reject new durable queue submissions while preserving verified accepted state

conditional.condition: the active profile requires privileged host resource mutations
conditional.failure_behavior: block privileged enforcement changes; do not bypass the broker

pressure_policy: reject new heavy work when capacity or enforceability is insufficient
terminate work only when the active envelope authorizes termination behavior

preserved: existing workloads with verified active controls
bounded work whose controls remain independently verifiable
low-risk work explicitly permitted without the missing observation
verified existing queue state when readable

failure_matrix.condition: Governance Policy Runtime unavailable for a required override
receipt persistence unavailable for a receipt-before-commit transition
hard memory, process, or storage pressure threatens core integrity

preserved: existing kernel or platform controls that remain independently active
bounded low-risk reading and recovery permitted by owning component contracts
current verified controls until reconciliation completes

recovery_preconditions: the active profile and overlays resolve
active envelope identities and versions resolve
running workload identities reconcile with allocation state
orphaned or escaped workloads are isolated
reservations and leases reconcile with actual execution
queue items reconcile for durability, expiry, cancellation, duplication, and current authorization
resource observations are fresh enough for the declared workload classes
no workload is assumed controlled without verification

principles: separation of resource and policy authority
privilege_rules: Ordinary admission and scheduling logic runs without host-wide privilege.
Privileged resource-control operations use the profile-approved narrow broker or platform mechanism.
Resource Governor receives only the capability needed to bind and control declared workload executions.
A privileged control path cannot grant business authorization or read workload payloads.
Failed privilege verification blocks the affected control operation.
privacy_rules: Usage observations contain resource metadata rather than workload business content.
Per-user and per-tenant resource records are access-controlled.
Logs omit secrets, payload data, and unrelated command arguments.
Retention is limited to operational, incident, billing when applicable, and conformance needs.
Selective audit records the decision and relevant resource facts without indiscriminate workload disclosure.

release_and_artifacts.release_set_rule: The active Resource Governor runtime and active resource envelope versions must satisfy declared compatibility constraints in the active Release Set or an explicitly permitted independent-channel compatibility declaration.
activation_rules: runtime and envelope candidates are validated before activation
resource envelope activation is staged and atomic
the previous verified envelope remains available for rollback
existing workloads are reconciled before a new envelope becomes authoritative
a stricter envelope defines explicit handling for currently running workloads
an incompatible runtime and envelope combination cannot admit new work
receipts: runtime activation receipt when classified as critical
forced termination receipt when classified as critical
emergency degradation and recovery receipts when required

logging_rules: Events use stable envelope, request, allocation, queue, and execution identifiers.
Logs distinguish observed usage from configured limits.
Logs do not contain workload business payloads.
A missing observation is not logged as zero usage.
Health does not report ready until envelope, adapter, and allocation reconciliation checks pass.
Critical transitions link to applicable receipt identifiers.

required_test_categories: resource envelope schema and target validation
rollback to the previous verified envelope
queue expiry, cancellation, retry, and authorization reevaluation
Resource Governor and Governance Policy Runtime separation
recovery reconciliation of workloads, queues, reservations, and controls
required_evidence_categories: runtime and envelope compatibility test result
conformance.conformance_claim: A deployment may claim Resource Governor conformance only for the active profile, supported resource dimensions, enforcement adapters, and workload classes covered by passing tests and retained evidence.

contract_invariants.statement: Resource Governor is the deterministic authority for CPU, memory, I/O, concurrency, queues, scheduling, and process limits.
Resource Governor does not make authorization, disclosure, consent, privilege, or exception decisions.
Resource availability never grants business authority.
Resource Governor does not write into workload-owned authoritative data stores.
Profile-specific resource mechanisms and thresholds do not become global implementation requirements.
A more specific resource envelope may restrict but cannot weaken an enclosing hard boundary.
Resource envelope activation never creates partial authoritative state.
Failed envelope or runtime activation preserves the previous verified state.
A Release Set preserves compatibility between the services runtime and governance envelopes.
Independent service or governance updates remain within declared compatibility constraints.
